description: Every valid email has a local name and domain name separated by @. In the local name, . is ignored and everything after + is ignored. Given a list of emails, return the number of unique addresses that actually receive mail.
intuition: The problem is just string normalization. Clean each email by removing dots and everything after '+' in the local part, then use a set to count unique results. The cleaning rules are straightforward string operations.
approach: For each email, split into local and domain parts. In the local part, remove dots and truncate at +. Combine with domain and add to a set. Return the set size.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: emails = ["test.email+alex@leetcode.com","test.e.mail+bob@leetcode.com","testemail@lee.tcode.com"]

Email 1: "test.email+alex@leetcode.com"
  local="test.email+alex", domain="leetcode.com"
  before +: "test.email"
  remove dots: "testemail"
  normalized: "testemail@leetcode.com"

Email 2: "test.e.mail+bob@leetcode.com"
  local="test.e.mail+bob", before +: "test.e.mail"
  remove dots: "testemail"
  normalized: "testemail@leetcode.com" (duplicate!)

Email 3: "testemail@lee.tcode.com"
  normalized: "testemail@lee.tcode.com" (different domain)

Set size = 2
explanation:
1. Split each email into local and domain parts at @.
2. In the local part, take only the portion before + and remove all dots.
3. Reconstruct the cleaned email and add to a set.
4. The set automatically handles duplicates.
5. Return the size of the set.
timeComplexity: O(n * k) where k is the average email length
hints: Split each email at @ to get local and domain.
In the local part, ignore everything after + and remove dots.
Use a set to track unique cleaned emails.
